title: FACS Sorting and Genome Amplification of Single Cells
author: Claudia Bergin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kbzcsp6
materials: Add 0,75 µl lysis reagents on the rim of the wells in each row using a multichannel pipette. Close the plate with a sealing and spin down. Put the plate in a thermocycler at 65° C for 10 min. Add 0,75 µl stop solution on the rim of the in each row using a multichannel pipette. Close the plate with sealing and spin down.

Add 10 µl of MDA-mix reagents on the rim of the wells in each row using a multichannel pipette. Close the plate with a sealing and spin down. Put the plate in a qPCR machine or a plate reader and incubate the plate at 30 °C for 8 h while reading the fluorescence every 15 minutes. The reaction is inactivated at 3 min 65 °C

Screening of whole genome amplification (WGA) products is done using the ROCHE lightCycler 480 and the ROCHE kit LightCycler 480 SYBR Green I Master in 10 ul reactions. Dilute PCR products x 100 and add 2 ul of the DNA to the PCR-mix including the forward and reverse primer. Add a melting curve analysis after the PCR cycling for evaluation of positive reactions by comparing Tm-values of the samples and positive as well as negative controls.

Purified PCR-products or WGA can be quantified in a plate format using the Quant-IT PicoGreen® dsDNA Assay kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and a plate reader as described in the REPLI-g Single Cell handbook from Qiagen Appendix B (2).

steps.title: Prepare cleanroom PPE and decontaminate
steps.instruction: Wear shoe covers, a dedicated lab coat (only inside the cleanroom), hair net, mouth cover, and fresh gloves for every entry; wipe all work surfaces, pipettes and any items that will enter the MDA hood with DNA AWAY®; clean gloves and equipment with DNA AWAY® before use.

steps.title: Prepare PBS‑filled 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Pipette 1 µl sterile filtered 1× PBS into each well of a 96‑well plate, cover with a clear sealing, UV‑treat the sealed plate for 2 J, and keep the plate at 4 °C until sorting later the same day.

steps.title: Prepare and stain cell suspension
steps.instruction: Thaw the cell sample on ice, pass it through a 70 µm cell strainer to remove aggregates, run an unstained aliquot for analysis, dilute the sample according to the measured event rate (eps), add SYBR Green I to a final 1× concentration, and stain the sample in the dark on ice for at least 20 min.

steps.title: Define sorting layout and controls
steps.instruction: During analysis of the stained sample, select the region of interest for sorting, define the sort layout in the CyClone plate layout, and include several empty wells as negative controls and wells containing multiple cells (e.g., 10 cells) as positive controls.

steps.title: Clean sort chamber and workspace
steps.instruction: Clean the sort chamber and surrounding workspace with a DNA AWAY® decontamination solution.

steps.title: Load plate and perform sorting
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the sealing from the prepared plate, place the plate in the sort chamber with correct orientation, start the sample flow and initiate the sort; after sorting, immediately reseal the plate, spin it down, and transfer it to a freezer (store at –20 °C for short‑term or –80 °C for long‑term storage). Repeat for additional plates as needed.

steps.title: Prepare PCR hood and ice boxes
steps.instruction: Wipe the PCR hood work area and all pipettes with DNA AWAY®, then UV‑irradiate the hood for 20–30 min; set up an ice‑box with ice and a lid wrapped in foil (for the UV‑linker) and a second ice‑box with ice for later reagent handling.

steps.title: Prepare lysis, stop, and MDA reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw plates on ice in the ice‑box; add lysis buffer (Buffer D2) to an 8‑well strip and close with an 8‑cap lid, repeat for the stop solution; mix all MDA reagents including the SYTO13 dye, distribute them into an 8‑well strip, close, and keep protected from light.

steps.title: Set up MDA reaction and monitor
steps.instruction: In the PCR hood, change tips between every well (or rows/columns if using a multichannel pipette); spin down all reagents, keep them on ice, and keep the polymerase in a cooling block; open sorted plates only in the hood, add lysis and neutralization reagents to each well, then add the REPLI‑g Single Cell MDA master mix (scaled to 12.5 µl total, i.e., one‑quarter of the handbook volume) without UV‑treating the master mix; seal the plate with an optical seal, protect from light with foil, and monitor fluorescence every 15 min at 30 °C for 8 h using SYTO13 on a PCR machine or plate reader.

steps.title: Implement contamination control during MDA
steps.instruction: Include negative controls such as “no sort” and no‑template controls; keep all reagents on ice after thawing, store tubes, water, lysis and stop solutions under UV for 2 J before use (master mix must not be UV‑treated); after adding SYTO13, keep the MDA master mix protected from light with foil.
